connect.title: Connect your site
connect.intro: Autoblog publishes your articles through a public, read-only JSON API. Your website fetches them from there and shows them in your own design. No database access, no SDK to install.

how.title: How it works
how.one: Autoblog writes and schedules articles. Only articles whose publication date has passed are public.
how.two: Your site calls the API below to get the list of articles, or a single article.
how.three: You display the title, image and content in your own layout.

base.title: Your API address
base.description: This is the address of this Autoblog instance. Use it from your site.

endpoints.title: Endpoints
endpoints.tryItHint: Opens the list of published articles.

list.order: Only published articles are returned: drafts and scheduled articles stay private until their date.

params.tag: Optional. Only return articles with this tag.

single.description: One article by its slug. Returns 404 if it doesn't exist or isn't published yet.
single.fields: On top of the list fields, it includes contentHtml (sanitized HTML, ready to display), contentMarkdown (if you prefer to render it yourself), readingTimeMinutes and updatedAt.

snippets.title: Copy-paste snippets
snippets.description: Start from one of these, then adapt the markup and styles to your site.

js.description: A single HTML file: it shows the list of articles, and an article when the address ends with ?slug=… No build step needed.

next.description: Two App Router pages: the blog index and an article page. They fetch on the server with revalidate: 300, so your site stays fast and always fresh.

notes.title: Good to know

cors.title: CORS (requests from a browser)
cors.body: By default the API accepts requests from any website. To restrict it, set PUBLIC_API_ALLOWED_ORIGINS to a comma-separated list of your sites (for example https://www.example.com) and redeploy. Requests made from a server, such as a Next.js page, are not affected by CORS.

cache.title: Caching
cache.body: Responses are cached for 5 minutes by CDNs and browsers (Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600). A newly published article can take a few minutes to appear on your site.

notes.seo: For SEO, use metaTitle and metaDescription for your page's title and description, coverImageUrl for social previews, and publishedAt and updatedAt in your structured data.
